editorial:
My Favorite Brunette is a 1947 comedy-thriller in which a baby photographer gets caught up in espionage after he agrees to run a neighbor's private investigation business. It stars Bob Hope and Dorothy Lamour. The queue marks it as a likely case of renewal absence, which would make the film itself free to reuse. This session could not confirm that.

The Stanford renewal database returned nothing readable, and the Catalog of Copyright Entries was not checked line by line. Until someone searches the 1974-1976 renewal entries by hand, every layer here stays undetermined. Do not treat the many copies on the Internet Archive as proof of status. Uploads there say nothing about whether the copyright was renewed. The score and the underlying story have not been checked either.
faq: Is My Favorite Brunette in the public domain?

Not confirmed. A 1947 film is public domain only if its copyright was never renewed in the 28th-year window (1974-1976). That check is not complete here. Search the renewal records linked in this dossier before reusing it.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy?
The copy exists and is watchable. Its being online does not clear it. Confirm the renewal status first, then check the score and the source story separately, because a film is not one copyright.
